title: Shape of a distribution
keyIdea: The shape of a histogram tells a story about the data. Symmetric data has two matching sides, and its mean and median are about the same. Skewed data has a long thin tail on one side, and the skew is named after the tail: a tail to the right is positive skew, a tail to the left is negative skew. The mean is pulled towards the tail, so it is usually above the median for positive skew and below it for negative skew. Bimodal data has two peaks, which usually means two groups are mixed together.
familyTip: Ask everyone in the family (or a group chat) how many minutes they spent getting to school or work today, and sketch the results as a tally or bar chart. Is there a long tail of slow trips? Would the mean or the median give a fairer typical time?

visual.caption: Which shape would each histogram have? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: Number of goals in a match
Marks on a very easy test
Heights of pupils and teachers together
Parkrun times of runners and walkers

lab.caption: Flagship lab: name six shapes, drag bars to build a skew and watch the mean chase the tail, split one hump into two peaks, match real data, spot the mean.

kid: A histogram shows how data is spread out. Its outline has a shape, and the shape has a name. If the left and right halves match like a mirror, the data is symmetric.

Sometimes most values bunch up on one side and a few values trail off a long way. That long thin part is the tail, and the data is skewed. Name the skew after the tail. A tail to the right is positive skew. A tail to the left is negative skew.

The mean uses every value, so the far values in the tail drag it along. In positive skew the mean is usually bigger than the median. In negative skew it is usually smaller. For skewed data the median is often the fairer typical value.
A chart with two separate peaks is bimodal. It usually means two groups are mixed, like runners and walkers in one race. Split the data into the two groups and each one has its own peak.
adult: Ages 14 to 16. US Common Core asks students to compare the shape, centre and spread of data sets and to explain how shape and extreme values affect them (HSS-ID.A.2 and A.3). AQA GCSE Statistics names symmetrical, positive and negative skew. Key words: distribution, histogram, symmetric, positive skew, negative skew, tail, bimodal, mean, median.

Skew is about the tail, not the peak: positive (right) skew has the mode on the left and a long right tail, as with incomes, house prices and goals per match. Negative (left) skew has a long left tail, as with age at death or marks on an easy test. The mean is usually on the tail side of the median, but this is a rule of thumb: for some discrete or bimodal data it fails.

A common mistake is to name the skew after the side where the peak is, which gives the opposite answer. Students also assume the mean and median are always close, or read two peaks as a mistake in the data rather than a sign of two groups. Another slip is to quote the mean as the typical value for strongly skewed data.

In the lab your child names the shape of six histograms, drags bars to build positive, negative and symmetric shapes while live mean and median lines move, slides one group's parkrun times away from another's until the chart splits into two peaks, matches real data sets to shapes, and picks out the mean on skewed charts.

practice.prompt: Five travel times, in minutes: 2, 3, 3, 4 and {=5*a-12}. What is the mean time, in minutes?
practice.hint: Add the five times and divide by 5.
practice.explain: Total = 2 + 3 + 3 + 4 + {=5*a-12} = {=5*a}, and {=5*a} ÷ 5 = {a} minutes. One long trip makes a tail to the right.

practice.prompt: The same five times: 2, 3, 3, 4 and {=5*a-12} minutes have a mean of {a}. How many minutes bigger is the mean than the median?
practice.hint: The median is the middle value of the five when they are in order.
practice.explain: The median is the 3rd value, 3 minutes. The mean is {a}, so it is {=a-3} minutes bigger: the long time in the tail pulls the mean up, but not the median.

practice.prompt: A histogram has its peak on the right and a long tail stretching to the left. What is its shape?
practice.hint: Name the skew after the tail, not the peak.
practice.explain: The tail is on the left, the negative end of the scale, so it is negative skew. The peak being on the right is what makes people say positive by mistake.

practice.prompt: A shop records how long customers spend inside. The histogram has two clear peaks, at 3 minutes and at 25 minutes. What is the best explanation?
choices: Two kinds of customer, such as quick buyers and browsers
The data has been recorded wrongly
practice.hint: What does a peak tell you about a group?
practice.explain: Two peaks usually mean two groups with different typical times. Averaging them gives 14 minutes, which hardly anyone spends.

practice.prompt: Pay in a company is positively skewed, with a few very high salaries. Which average best describes a typical worker's pay?
practice.hint: Which average is pulled by the few very high salaries?
practice.explain: The few large salaries in the right tail drag the mean up. The median is the middle worker's pay, so it shows a typical worker better.

pool.prompt: Seven yearly pay values, in £1000s: 18, 20, 21, 22, 24, 26 and {=7*a-131}. What is the mean, in £1000s?
pool.hint: Add all seven values and divide by 7.

pool.prompt: The pay values 18, 20, 21, 22, 24, 26 and {=7*a-131} (in £1000s) have a mean of {a}. How far is the mean above the median, in £1000s?
pool.hint: The median is the 4th of the seven values in order.
pool.explain: The median is 22, so the mean is {a} − 22 = {=a-22} above it. The one high salary makes a right tail that pulls only the mean.

pool.prompt: Which data set is most likely to be negatively skewed?
choices: Ages of people at death in the UK
pool.hint: Look for data where most values are high and a few are low.
pool.explain: Most people die old and a few die young, so the long tail is on the left. Pay and pets have a few very large values, a right tail.

pool.prompt: A distribution is symmetric with one peak. What can you say about its mean and median?
pool.hint: With matching sides, is anything pulling the mean one way?
pool.explain: With matching sides no tail pulls the mean, so the mean and median sit together in the middle.

pool.prompt: For a set of data the mean is 48 and the median is 35. What shape is the distribution most likely to be?
pool.hint: The mean is pulled towards the tail. Which side is the mean on?
pool.explain: The mean is well above the median, so something is pulling it up: a tail of high values. That is positive skew.

pool.prompt: Heights of everyone at a primary school, pupils and staff, are drawn as one histogram. What shape do you expect?
pool.hint: How many groups with different typical heights are mixed?
pool.explain: Children and adults each have their own typical height, so the chart has two peaks: bimodal.

pool.prompt: Jo says a chart is positively skewed because its peak is on the right. What is her mistake?
choices: Skew is named after the tail, so a peak on the right means negative skew
Skew is named after the peak, so she is right
Skew depends only on the tallest bar's height
pool.hint: Where is the long thin tail if the peak is on the right?
pool.explain: If the peak is on the right, the tail stretches to the left, so it is negative skew. Always look for the tail.

pool.prompt: Marks on a very hard test bunch near zero with a few high scores. Which statement is true?
choices: It is positively skewed and the mean is likely above the median
It is negatively skewed and the mean is likely above the median
It is symmetric, so the mean equals the median
pool.hint: Where are most marks, and which way does the tail go?
pool.explain: Most marks are low and a few are high, so the tail is on the right: positive skew. The high marks pull the mean above the median.
